warnings: Quiz language appears sparse; make assessment prompts explicit.

improvement_notes: Remove the sentence beginning “An illustrator could show this...” because the lesson already provides generated visuals and the sentence reads like an internal production note.

Reduce repeated explanations of straight-line distance, map accuracy, and coordinate-versus-frame distinctions. The technical caveats are valuable, but several are restated in multiple sections and increase cognitive load.

Add a brief explicit learning check immediately after the first coordinate examples, such as asking students to plot and label one positive-quadrant and one negative-quadrant point before introducing distance.
The Python lab is strong, but students would benefit from a short expected-output block showing representative console results before they run the program.
Clarify that the plotted circle represents a locus of points five units from RoboRover, not a physical sensor range or guaranteed reachable area.

The real-robot section introduces world and body frames accurately, but a small two-frame diagram or a one-sentence rotation example would make the distinction more concrete without requiring advanced transformation mathematics.
Consider adding a physical RoboRover activity using tape and floor markers so students can connect coordinate signs, scale, and map-frame location to an actual robot or classroom layout.

The “Further Learning” section provides search terms but no curated sources. Either retain it explicitly as an unguided search activity or replace it with verified, stable references before publication.
